subject: physics
title: Required practicals: thermal physics
key_idea: Specific latent heat is found from the electrical energy supplied and the mass that changed phase. Boyle's law is tested with a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature: pressure is inversely proportional to volume.

sections.heading: Specific latent heat of a phase change

blocks.text: This practical finds the energy needed to change 1 kg of a substance from one phase to another, using an electric heater.

items.text: Put an immersion heater in a well-insulated container of the substance on a balance, for example water just at its boiling point. For melting, put the heater in ice in a funnel above a beaker.
Switch on the heater, and read the potential difference V and current I. Start a stopwatch.
After a set time t, find the mass of substance that changed phase: the mass lost as steam, or the mass of melted ice collected.
For melting, repeat with the heater off for the same time to find the mass of ice melted by the room, and subtract it. For boiling, use the gradient of a graph instead.
Repeat for different times or powers, and average the values of L.

blocks.label: Specific latent heat
where: L is the specific latent heat (J kg⁻¹)
V is the potential difference across the heater (V)
I is the current in the heater (A)
Δm is the mass that changed phase, corrected for the control (kg)

items: A graph of electrical energy VIt against mass changed Δm is a straight line. Its **gradient** is L.
Energy lost to the surroundings makes the measured L too large when boiling, so insulate the container.
Take care with hot water, steam and the heater: keep mains leads away from water and never switch the heater on in air.
Find L from the electrical energy supplied and the mass that changed phase.
Use a control run, or a gradient, to remove the effect of energy losses.

sections.heading: Pressure and volume of a gas at fixed temperature

blocks.text: This practical shows that the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume when the temperature is constant.

diagram.alt: Put the steps of the Boyle's law practical in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps of the practical in the correct order.
steps: Trap a fixed mass of air in a sealed tube above oil, connected to a pressure gauge and a pump.
Read the initial pressure and the length of the air column.
Use the pump to change the pressure slowly.
Wait for the temperature to settle, then read the new pressure and length.
Repeat for a range of pressures, then plot the results.

items: The tube has a uniform cross-section, so the volume V is proportional to the length of the air column.
Change the pressure slowly and wait each time, so the temperature of the air stays the same as the room.
Plot a graph of p against 1 / V. A straight line through the origin shows that p ∝ 1 / V, so pV is constant.
Check by calculating pV for each reading; the values should agree within the uncertainty.

diagram.alt: Pressure against one over volume for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature. A straight line through the origin.

items: Compression warms a gas, which is why the pressure must be changed slowly.
Do not go beyond the maximum pressure of the gauge or the tube. Wear eye protection, in case the tube fails.
At constant temperature, p ∝ 1 / V, so a graph of p against 1 / V is a straight line through the origin.
Change the pressure slowly so the temperature stays constant.

checks.q: In an electrical experiment to find the specific latent heat of vaporisation of water, 0.015 kg of water is boiled away in 600 s by a 50 W heater. Calculate the specific latent heat. Assume no energy losses.
Describe how to show that the pressure and volume of a fixed mass of gas are inversely proportional at constant temperature.
checks.a: Trap a fixed mass of gas, change its pressure, and record the pressure and volume each time, waiting for the temperature to settle. Plot p against 1/V and obtain a straight line through the origin, or show that pV is constant.

checks.q: Explain why the pressure in the gas experiment should be changed slowly.
checks.a: Compressing a gas does work on it and warms it. Changing the pressure slowly gives time for the gas to return to room temperature.
